comments.text: Uses X as a sound selector. Copies six bytes of stream pointers from $0C20 into $03B4-$03B9 and the mode byte from $0C14 into $0495. Clears the voice state and writes the initial volume and envelope registers.
Returns while the guard at $048E is nonzero. Otherwise it traverses three SID voices using the stream pointers at $03B4 and $03B7.
Twelve mode bytes indexed by X in the sound initializer; $0419 writes the selected mode into the immediate operand at $0495.
Selector 0: the three stream addresses are $0F00, $0FA8, $0FEC. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 1: the three stream addresses are $13C3, $13C6, $13D2. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 2: the three stream addresses are $148B, $148D, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 3: the three stream addresses are $149C, $149F, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 4: the three stream addresses are $14A7, $1517, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 5: the three stream addresses are $14AF, $1517, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 6: the three stream addresses are $14BA, $1517, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 7: the three stream addresses are $14C5, $14C7, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 8: the three stream addresses are $14EF, $1517, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 9: the three stream addresses are $14F7, $1517, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 10: the three stream addresses are $1502, $1517, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 11: the three stream addresses are $040C, $0409, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Jumps to the new-game setup at $2C11. The following bytes starting at $2C03 are mutable gameplay state.
Current level resource index. Setup at $2C11 begins at zero. The transition at $63B7 uses 0 through 5 as the disk selector and sends 6 to the ending path.
Resets the resource index, takes the title's selection from $1A63 minus one into $2F0A, calls common score and life setup, then falls through to level setup.

Resets the level's gameplay state, copies the initial actor sprite pointers, sets up video and the level initialisation calls, then installs the hardware IRQ at $2D5E and enters the main loop at $5FE5. The disk transition at $63C2 enters here without resetting the resource index.
Saves A, Y and X and acknowledges the VIC interrupt. Dispatches the four states 0 to 3 from zero-page $34 to $308E, $319C, $3252 or $32C0; other values take the longer update starting at $2D8F.
When $2C04 is nonnegative, starts that sound through $040E and then writes $80 to mark the request handled. On the negative path calls the regular SID update at $048D instead.
Four vertical positions. The drawing order compares these at $2F22, and the first set of sprite layers uses them as the VIC Y coordinates.
Four actor indices sorted by vertical position at $2F11. Adjacent entries with equal Y keep their order.
Four bytes per actor in sixteen bytes. The first two give the overlaid shapes above the waist and the second two give the shapes below it.
Low eight bits of four actor X positions. Port 2's right branch increments the first actor's value twice, subject to movement checks.
Zero after moving left through $350A, one after moving right through $35A4. The fire dispatcher reads this to choose between two direction dispatches.
Attack or movement state for the first actor. $4417 doubles it to select a routine from the little-endian jump table starting at $442B.
Port 1's fire dispatcher stores the second actor's state here. For example, $4B15 stores $01 for left and fire when the second actor faces left.
Sorts four actor indices by nondecreasing Y, then copies each actor's four sprite pointers into $24–$33 and two colour values into $35–$3C in that order.

Schedules each upper-to-lower sprite change at actor Y plus 19, capped at $D5. Holds the new sprite Y two lines below that scheduled time. Later comparisons adjust the schedule when changes are close together.

Places four sprite pairs at the sorted actor coordinates. Each pair uses matching X and Y and writes pointers in both graphics screen buffers. Separate pointer pairs are installed during the raster changes.
Writes a common Y to sprites 0 and 1, a common X from $2EEC,Y, and the pair of shape pointers at $30 and $31 to both screen buffers.

Reads CIA 1 port A for joystick 2. Tests fire before the direction comparisons when $344E is clear; otherwise advances the counter at $421A and clears the gate at $1B. The direction comparisons dispatch the selected direction or diagonal.

Reads CIA 1 port B for joystick 1. Tests fire before the direction comparisons when $344F is clear; otherwise advances the counter at $421B and clears the gate at $1B. The direction comparisons dispatch the selected direction or diagonal.
Starts the fire gate. On level resource 3 it checks four background tile IDs before dispatching. For eligible positions, it checks the facing byte and one of nine port-2 direction and fire values.
Clears the attack counter at $2F03 and compares the port with neutral fire or one of eight directions. The handlers select action IDs, with some choices consulting the weapon variable at $2F00.

Compares the same nine port-2 values as the left-facing dispatcher. The branches choose right-facing attack states. Both facings use $12 for up-right and $11 for up-left, and preserve the actor's initial Y for those jumps.
Reads a pointer from the table at $442B and patches the absolute JMP at $4428. The table index is twice the action ID at $2F02.
Little-endian routine addresses. The first entry is $4459 and the next is $447D, for action IDs 0 and 1.
Port 1 variant of the fire dispatcher. Uses the second actor's position and counter, tests its facing at $2EFB, and checks the joystick values through CIA1 port B.
Increments the current resource index and raises the request flag checked at $5FED.
Horizontal camera offset in character columns. Horizontal scrolling adjusts the map pointer at $02/$03 by a byte as it changes this count.
Vertical camera offset in character rows. Vertical scrolling adjusts the map pointer at $02/$03 by 240 bytes for each count in either direction.
The main loop at $5FED routes to the level transition when this byte is nonzero.
The main loop at $5FE5 checks this before the level transition. A nonzero value sends it to $63C5 to reload the title.
Clears level update flags and counters, selects and initialises video state, and resets timer digits at $6124/$6125 to 7 and 0.
Increments the camera row and advances the 16-bit map pointer by 240 bytes.
Decrements the camera row and subtracts 240 from the 16-bit map pointer.

Writes the fine-scroll values and screen selection to VIC. When the phase count reaches eight and the ready flag is set, flips the buffer, requests the next main-loop draw, and updates $D018 for the new screen.
Indexes the map pointers at $5FD3 by twice the level number. Copies the pointer to zero page $02/$03. Writes the level's two shared VIC multicolour values from $5FC7/$5FCD and sets $5B3A from $5FDF.
Six values indexed by $2C05, written to VIC register $D022 by $5FB7.
Six values indexed by $2C05, written to VIC register $D023 by $5FBD.
Six little-endian starting window pointers. The six levels start at $9000, $A2C0, $9000, $9D20, $9000 and $9000 respectively.
Six initial values written to $5B3A by $5FC3. The subsequent use of that byte needs checking.

Checks game over at $5B61 before level change at $5B60. Otherwise waits on the update request at $5B42, clears it, calls the shared routine at $1AFA, refreshes the HUD, updates the timer and enemy logic, and draws the background into the selected screen buffer.

Copies 24 rows of 40 character codes from ($04) into ($06), advancing the source by 240 and the destination by 40 per row. Uses each character code to index $8E00 and stores the result through ($08), which the caller sets for the colour buffer.
Turns off sprites and switches the VIC display matrix in the lower screen area. Changes raster-dependent rows and scroll bits through $D011, $D016 and $D018, with two timed waits between writes.

After the flag at $5B57 is set, advances $5B58 through 256 offsets. At each offset copies one byte from each of eight pages at $8600-$8DFF to the active font at $C800-$CFFF and one replacement colour from $8F00 to $8E00. Clears the flag on wrap.
When $5B5B is nonzero, decrements it, restores $5B59 to five and clears $2F00; otherwise requests the state at $5B5D.
When $5B5C is nonzero, decrements it, restores $5B5A to five and clears $2F01; otherwise requests the state at $5B5E.
Fills health blocks, draws the scores and life digits from their stored values, and writes the respective screen-code glyphs into the status panel.
Counts calls modulo 50 using $5B5F. On each rollover it subtracts one decimal digit from $6125, borrows from $6124 when needed, and on borrowing below 00 resets to 70 before calling $617D and $619F.
Sets the replacement flag $5B57 at column $4D of L0 or column $35 of L1. Other level indices return without this test.
Reads the level resource index. For indices before 6 calls the disk transition with that selector, re-enables interrupts and jumps to level setup at $2C20. At 6 it instead takes the ending path.
Requests file-table index 6 (IN) from $1960, then re-enables interrupts and jumps to the title at $1A60. The TO driver also shows GAME OVER on this path.
Requests index 9 (ED), then selects processor-port value $36, enables interrupts and jumps to $B500.

Odd sprite for the lower half of the player in the opening pose captured after walking right. Pointer $A2 in VIC bank $C000. Its double-width pixels use the actor's lower-half colour and two shared colours.
Even sprite for the lower half of the same player pose. Pointer $A3 selects the 24-pixel-wide black overlay at the same X and Y.
Odd sprite for the upper half of the player in the opening pose captured after walking right. Pointer $B8 selects the multicolour figure underneath its high-resolution outline.
Even sprite for the upper half of the same player pose. Pointer $B9 selects the overlay using the sprite's own black colour.
